fact: The Lead drafts one candidate; the members identify missed obligations, false passes or conflicts.
Each implementation step identifies its starting point, intended outcome and observable acceptance check.
The Lead signs the exact version approved by both members or asks the user to resolve a decision outside Design authority.
On a revised candidate, check changed passages, related effects, and the Lead response to earlier findings.
Identify the evidence that distinguishes the options, report the answer and its basis, and return to the interrupted Work State.
A blocking finding names its Goal, Delivery or step ID, counterexample, evidence and proposed correction. The Lead records a resolution for each finding.

When an implementer escalates an ownership question, trace one affected input to the state writer and result consumer. Give actionable direction within the approved plan and name what would invalidate the boundary judgment.

When a named designer finds a conflict between a task fact and project background, check each record’s owner project, revision, and authority. Give the lead both retrievable records and the design decision affected.
